Description

The μ-opioid receptor sits on peptidergic nociceptors, at their peripheral endings in the joint and their central terminals in the dorsal horn. Opioid peptides released by immune cells and opioid drugs activate it, and Gi/o proteins then inhibit adenylate cyclase while the Gβγ subunits open GIRK potassium channels and close N-type calcium channels. The neuron becomes less excitable and releases less glutamate and substance P. Naloxone and naltrexone bind the same receptor without activating it and so block these actions. In knee and hip OA, opioid drugs give only a small reduction of pain.
